meta.title: Who originally recorded "I Will Always Love You"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not a Whitney Houston original. "I Will Always Love You" was written and first recorded by Dolly Parton in 1974 on RCA Victor. Houston’s 1992 version from The Bodyguard is a cover — a cover that outsold the original many times over.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'I Will Always Love You'?
meta.ogDescription: Everyone thinks it’s Whitney’s song. It’s a 1974 Dolly Parton single — she wrote it herself as a farewell to her mentor. Houston’s 1992 cover just eclipsed it.

answer.label: Not a Whitney original — a 1974 Dolly Parton song
answer.originalArtistDates: b. 1946 · American country singer and songwriter
answer.sourceLine: This is one of pop’s great cover-eclipses: almost everyone takes ‘I Will Always Love You’ for a Whitney Houston original, but Houston’s 1992 version is a cover. The song was written and first recorded by Dolly Parton in 1974 on RCA Victor — a country No. 1 she wrote herself as a farewell to her mentor Porter Wagoner. Houston picked it up eighteen years later for The Bodyguard and turned it into one of the best-selling singles ever made.

original.label: RCA Victor
original.released: Written in 1973 and recorded by Parton; released as a single on 11 March 1974
original.charted: Reached No. 1 on the US Billboard Hot Country Songs chart — and did so again in 1982 with a re-recording for The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas
original.writer: Dolly Parton (who also recorded it first)
original.cover: Whitney Houston — recorded 22 April 1992, released 2 November 1992 on Arista Records, from the soundtrack to The Bodyguard. It spent a then-record 14 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the best-selling singles of all time.
trail: The song was written by Dolly Parton in 1973 and first recorded by her; RCA Victor released it as a single on 11 March 1974 Wikipedia ↗.

Parton wrote it as a farewell to Porter Wagoner, her business partner and mentor, as she moved to strike out on her own. Her original went to No. 1 on the country chart — and did it a second time in 1982 with a re-recording for a film soundtrack.

Whitney Houston recorded her version in April 1992 for The Bodyguard and released it that November on Arista; it spent 14 weeks at No. 1 and eclipsed the original so thoroughly that most listeners now assume it began with her SecondHandSongs ↗.

authors.name: Dolly Parton
authors.kicker: The writer and original recording artist
authors.heading: About Dolly Parton
authors.metaLine: b. 1946 · American country singer and songwriter
authors.bio: Dolly Parton (b. 1946) is one of the most successful songwriters in American music, and she both wrote ‘I Will Always Love You’ and recorded it first, in 1974 for RCA Victor. She wrote it as a tender farewell to Porter Wagoner, the mentor whose show launched her, as she left to build a solo career. Because she kept her publishing — famously refusing to hand half of it to Elvis Presley’s camp — Whitney Houston’s later cover earned Parton a fortune in songwriter royalties; she has joked that it let her ‘buy Graceland.’

authors.name: Whitney Houston
authors.heading: Why it gets pinned on Whitney
authors.bio: Whitney Houston (1963–2012) recorded ‘I Will Always Love You’ in 1992 for The Bodyguard, and her towering, a-cappella-opening arrangement so completely redefined the song that it is now hers in the public mind. Her version spent a then-record 14 weeks at No. 1 and became one of the best-selling singles of all time. This is the rare misattribution where the cover is arguably the more famous record; the only error is forgetting there was an original at all — a country song Dolly Parton wrote and sang first.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: This is a generous kind of misattribution: Whitney Houston’s record really is a landmark, and for most listeners the definitive one. The only error is believing she originated the song — a 1992 cover mistaken for the source.

items.why: Houston’s 1992 version is a cover. Dolly Parton wrote the song and recorded it first, eighteen years earlier, in 1974 the history ↗.

items.tag: wrote it and recorded it first
items.why: Parton’s original was a country No. 1 — a real hit, but on the country chart rather than the pop mainstream, which is part of why the pop cover could overshadow it so completely.

items.tag: author, not just the first singer
items.why: Parton did not merely record it first — she wrote it. She also kept the publishing, so the cover that eclipsed her as a performer made her a fortune as its author.

misattribution.truthLine: Written and first recorded by Dolly Parton in 1974, and made famous — but not originated — by Whitney Houston in 1992 the record ↗.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: Most cover-eclipses happen because the original was obscure. ‘I Will Always Love You’ is different: Dolly Parton’s 1974 version was a genuine hit — a country No. 1, twice over — yet it still lost the song. Whitney Houston’s 1992 cover was not merely bigger; it crossed into the pop mainstream with a force the country original never had, and for a global audience it simply became the version.

The irony is that the eclipse enriched the woman it eclipsed. Because Parton wrote the song and held onto its publishing, Houston’s blockbuster cover paid Parton enormous songwriter royalties — more than her own recording ever could. The performer credit drifted to Houston; the authorship, and the cheque, stayed with Parton.
detailsBody: Dolly Parton writes ‘I Will Always Love You’ in 1973, as a farewell to Porter Wagoner.
Parton records it first; RCA Victor releases it 11 March 1974 → country No. 1.
Parton re-records it for The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas (1982) → country No. 1 again.
Whitney Houston records her version, 22 April 1992, for The Bodyguard.
Released 2 November 1992 on Arista → 14 weeks at Hot 100 No. 1; it becomes one of the best-selling singles ever, and the original fades from public memory.
context.pull: The cover eclipsed her as a performer — and, because she wrote it, made her a fortune as its author.
